# linked_list_allocator 0.10.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/linked_list_allocator/

# linked-list-allocator

## Usage

Create a static allocator in your root module:

```
use LockedHeap;
static ALLOCATOR: LockedHeap = empty;
```
Before using this allocator, you need to init it:

```
```
## Features

- `use_spin`- `LockedHeap`type that implements the- `GlobalAlloc`
- `alloc_ref`- `AllocRef`- Warning: The `AllocRef`trait is still regularly changed on the Rust side, so expect some regular breakage when using this feature.

- Warning: The

# linked_list_allocator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/linked_list_allocator/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/linked_list_allocator/

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html)
- A fixed size heap backed by a linked list of free memory blocks.
- [Locked](https://docs.rs/struct.LockedHeap.html)- Heap

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [align_](https://docs.rs/fn.align_down_size.html)- down_ - size
- Align downwards. Returns the greatest x with alignment `align`so that x <= addr. The alignment must be a power of 2.
- [align_](https://docs.rs/fn.align_up.html)- up
- Align upwards. Returns the smallest x with alignment `align`so that x >= addr. The alignment must be a power of 2.
- [align_](https://docs.rs/fn.align_up_size.html)- up_ - size

### use_spin (default)

### spinning_top (default)

### alloc_ref

This feature flag does not enable additional features.

### const_mut_refs

This feature flag does not enable additional features.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# linked_list_allocator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/linked-list-allocator

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html)
- A fixed size heap backed by a linked list of free memory blocks.
- [Locked](https://docs.rs/struct.LockedHeap.html)- Heap

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [align_](https://docs.rs/fn.align_down_size.html)- down_ - size
- Align downwards. Returns the greatest x with alignment `align`so that x <= addr. The alignment must be a power of 2.
- [align_](https://docs.rs/fn.align_up.html)- up
- Align upwards. Returns the smallest x with alignment `align`so that x >= addr. The alignment must be a power of 2.
- [align_](https://docs.rs/fn.align_up_size.html)- up_ - size

# bamboo_storage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-storage/2026.7.3/bamboo_storage/

## Expand description

Session storage backends for Bamboo agents.

Provides persistent storage implementations:

- **JsonlStorage**: Simple JSON file per session
- **SessionStoreV2**: Folder-per-session layout with SQLite search index
- **SessionSearchIndex**: Full-text search for session content
- **merge_save_session**: Merge-aware session save with concurrent edit protection

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use jsonl::`- [JsonlStorage](https://docs.rs/jsonl/struct.JsonlStorage.html);
- `pub use search_index::`- [SessionSearchIndex](https://docs.rs/search_index/struct.SessionSearchIndex.html);
- `pub use search_index::`- [SessionSearchMatch](https://docs.rs/search_index/struct.SessionSearchMatch.html);
- `pub use session_merge::`- [merge_save_session](https://docs.rs/session_merge/fn.merge_save_session.html);
- `pub use session_merge::`- [LockedSessionStore](https://docs.rs/session_merge/struct.LockedSessionStore.html);
- `pub use v2::`- [CleanupMode](https://docs.rs/v2/enum.CleanupMode.html);
- `pub use v2::`- [CleanupResult](https://docs.rs/v2/struct.CleanupResult.html);
- `pub use v2::`- [SessionIndexEntry](https://docs.rs/v2/struct.SessionIndexEntry.html);
- `pub use v2::`- [SessionPlacement](https://docs.rs/v2/struct.SessionPlacement.html);
- `pub use v2::`- [SessionStoreV2](https://docs.rs/v2/struct.SessionStoreV2.html);
- `pub use v2::`- [SessionsIndex](https://docs.rs/v2/struct.SessionsIndex.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [jsonl](https://docs.rs/jsonl/index.html)
- JSONL-based session storage implementation.
- [search_](https://docs.rs/search_index/index.html)- index
- [session_](https://docs.rs/session_merge/index.html)- merge
- Merge-aware session save helper.
- [v2](https://docs.rs/v2/index.html)
- Session storage V2 (folder-per-session + global index).

# facett_app - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/facett-app/0.1.10/facett_app/

## Expand description

**facett-app** — the app-framework layer over facett’s components.

Turns a set of [ Facet](https://docs.rs/facett-core/0.1.10/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/facett_core/trait.Facet.html)s into a whole

*app*: a

[(one navigation model → many surfaces), a](https://docs.rs/nav/struct.NavModel.html)

`NavModel`[(route→view with back/forward, native + wasm-hash), and nav chrome (](https://docs.rs/router/struct.Router.html)

`Router`[,](https://docs.rs/sidebar/struct.Sidebar.html)

`Sidebar`[,](https://docs.rs/shell/fn.breadcrumb.html)

`breadcrumb`[). Immediate-mode, canvas-only, headless-addressable — the “facett way”.](https://docs.rs/shell/struct.NavShell.html)

`NavShell`This is **Fas 1** of the framework införandeplan
(`workspace_nordisk/facett-ramverk-inforandeplan.md`): the navigation & menu
backbone. `AppShell`, split-panes and the overlay system land in later phases.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use appshell::`- [AppShell](https://docs.rs/appshell/struct.AppShell.html);
- `pub use colorpicker::`- [ColorPicker](https://docs.rs/colorpicker/struct.ColorPicker.html);
- `pub use datepicker::`- [DatePicker](https://docs.rs/datepicker/struct.DatePicker.html);
- `pub use dropdown::`- [Dropdown](https://docs.rs/dropdown/struct.Dropdown.html);
- `pub use modal::`- [Modal](https://docs.rs/modal/struct.Modal.html);
- `pub use popover::`- [Popover](https://docs.rs/popover/struct.Popover.html);
- `pub use router::`- [Router](https://docs.rs/router/struct.Router.html);
- `pub use sidebar::`- [Sidebar](https://docs.rs/sidebar/struct.Sidebar.html);
- `pub use splitpane::`- [SplitPane](https://docs.rs/splitpane/struct.SplitPane.html);
- `pub use tabview::`- [TabView](https://docs.rs/tabview/struct.TabView.html);
- `pub use toast::`- [Level](https://docs.rs/toast/enum.Level.html);
- `pub use toast::`- [Toasts](https://docs.rs/toast/struct.Toasts.html);
- `pub use tree::`- [Tree](https://docs.rs/tree/struct.Tree.html);
- `pub use widgets::`- [Accordion](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Accordion.html);
- `pub use widgets::`- [Pagination](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Pagination.html);
- `pub use widgets::`- [Stepper](https://docs.rs/widgets/struct.Stepper.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [appshell](https://docs.rs/appshell/index.html)
- `AppShell`— compose a whole app from facett components.- `Sidebar`- `NavModel`- **real**+ a statusbar. Where- `Facet`- `NavShell`- `AppShell`mounts actual components — so the active route renders a grid, a chart, a 3D model, … swapped by navigation.
- [colorpicker](https://docs.rs/colorpicker/index.html)
- `ColorPicker`— a themed colour picker with preset swatches.- `state_json`).
- [datepicker](https://docs.rs/datepicker/index.html)
- `DatePicker`— a month calendar.- `chrono`/- `time`dep — day-of-week via Sakamoto’s algorithm, so it builds anywhere incl. wasm). The viewed month + selected date live in the struct (FC-1), headless (- `select`,- `prev_month`/- `next_month`), observable (- `state_json`).
- [dropdown](https://docs.rs/dropdown/index.html)
- `Dropdown`— a themed, headless select/combobox.- `egui::ComboBox`(which hides its open/closed state in egui memory, violating the component contract’s FC-1), this keeps- **all**state — including- `open`— in the struct, so it is headless-addressable (- `select`,- `set_open`) and fully observable (- `state_json`). Theme-aware; stable id.
- [menu](https://docs.rs/menu/index.html)
- **NavModel → facett-menu bridge.**Now that- `facett_menu::Command`takes owned ids, the- *same*- `NavModel`- `Command`- `id`is the route and whose- `group`is the parent section’s label.
- [modal](https://docs.rs/modal/index.html)
- `Modal`— a reusable dialog overlay.- `facett-menu`- `CommandPalette`pattern (a scrim + a centred panel at- `Order::Foreground`, Esc to dismiss) into an addressable dialog: a title + body + buttons. All state (incl.- `open`and the last action) lives in the struct (FC-1), so it is headless-drivable (- `open`/- `close`/- `take_action`) and observable (- `state_json`).
- [nav](https://docs.rs/nav/index.html)
- `NavModel`— one navigation model, many surfaces.- `NavItem`- `facett-menu`’s one- `Command`set drives its three surfaces today. Pure data + headless-addressable by id.
- [palette](https://docs.rs/palette/index.html)
- `NavPalette`— a fuzzy command palette over a- `NavModel`- `&'static`requirement, no leak) — the nav-model counterpart to- `facett-menu`’s static-command palette. State in the struct (FC-1); headless (- `invoke`).
- [popover](https://docs.rs/popover/index.html)
- `Popover`— an anchored floating panel.- `open`state lives in the struct (FC-1), so it is headless-drivable + observable.
- [router](https://docs.rs/router/index.html)
- `Router`— route → view, with history.- `set_active_by_title`+ the wasm- `#TabName`deep-link into a route stack with back/forward, usable native AND on wasm. A route is an opaque string id (matches a- `NavItem`
- [shell](https://docs.rs/shell/index.html)
- `NavShell`— sidebar + router + content, as one- `Facet`- `Sidebar`- `Router`- `AppShell`(Fas 2), and the demoable proof of the nav backbone.
- [sidebar](https://docs.rs/sidebar/index.html)
- `Sidebar`— a persistent nav rail rendered from a- `NavModel`- `look::Theme`). Returns the clicked route so the host drives its [- `Router`].
- [splitpane](https://docs.rs/splitpane/index.html)
- `SplitPane`— host two Facets with a draggable divider.- `Facet`- `state_json`folds in both children.
- [tabview](https://docs.rs/tabview/index.html)
- `TabView`— nested in-content tabs.- *inside*a pane (distinct from the deck’s top-level tabs): headers + an active id, with the caller drawing content for- `active()`. State in the struct (FC-1), headless (- `select`), observable (- `state_json`).
- [toast](https://docs.rs/toast/index.html)
- `Toasts`— a notification queue.- `tick(dt)`(injected in tests for determinism, FC-7; the ambient frame- `dt`in live use), so state stays in the struct (FC-1) and is observable (- `state_json`).
- [tree](https://docs.rs/tree/index.html)
- `Tree`— a hierarchical single-select navigator.- `NavModel`- **any**node is selectable (a data/object picker), distinct from- `Sidebar`- `select`), observable (- `state_json`).
- [widgets](https://docs.rs/widgets/index.html)
- **Input/data widgets (Fas 4).**Themed, headless-addressable primitives that add a semantic + observable layer over raw egui:- `Accordion`- `Stepper`- `Pagination`- `state_json`(FC-3).

# bamboo_metrics - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-metrics/2026.7.3/bamboo_metrics/

## Expand description

Live metrics pipeline for the Bamboo agent framework.

Holds the runtime metrics flow — event bus, collector, background worker and
aggregation — plus the `MetricsService` facade. The persistence layer
(metrics `types` and the `MetricsStorage` abstraction with its SQLite
implementation) lives in `bamboo_infrastructure::metrics` and is re-exported
here so callers see one cohesive `bamboo_metrics::…` surface.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use aggregator::`- [aggregate_monthly](https://docs.rs/aggregator/fn.aggregate_monthly.html);
- `pub use aggregator::`- [aggregate_weekly](https://docs.rs/aggregator/fn.aggregate_weekly.html);
- `pub use aggregator::`- [PeriodMetrics](https://docs.rs/aggregator/struct.PeriodMetrics.html);
- `pub use bus::`- [MetricsBus](https://docs.rs/bus/struct.MetricsBus.html);
- `pub use collector::`- [MetricsCollector](https://docs.rs/collector/struct.MetricsCollector.html);
- `pub use events::`- [ChatEvent](https://docs.rs/events/enum.ChatEvent.html);
- `pub use events::`- [EventMeta](https://docs.rs/events/struct.EventMeta.html);
- `pub use events::`- [ForwardEvent](https://docs.rs/events/enum.ForwardEvent.html);
- `pub use events::`- [MetricsEvent](https://docs.rs/events/enum.MetricsEvent.html);
- `pub use events::`- [SystemEvent](https://docs.rs/events/enum.SystemEvent.html);
- `pub use metrics_service::`- [MetricsService](https://docs.rs/metrics_service/struct.MetricsService.html);
- `pub use worker::`- [MetricsWorker](https://docs.rs/worker/struct.MetricsWorker.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [aggregator](https://docs.rs/aggregator/index.html)
- [bus](https://docs.rs/bus/index.html)
- [collector](https://docs.rs/collector/index.html)
- [events](https://docs.rs/events/index.html)
- Metrics Event System
- [metrics_](https://docs.rs/metrics_service/index.html)- service
- [storage](https://docs.rs/storage/index.html)
- Metrics Storage System
- [types](https://docs.rs/types/index.html)
- Metrics types for tracking agent performance and usage
- [worker](https://docs.rs/worker/index.html)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Daily](https://docs.rs/struct.DailyMetrics.html)- Metrics
- Aggregated metrics for a single day
- [Forward](https://docs.rs/struct.ForwardEndpointMetrics.html)- Endpoint - Metrics
- [Forward](https://docs.rs/struct.ForwardMetricsFilter.html)- Metrics - Filter
- [Forward](https://docs.rs/struct.ForwardMetricsSummary.html)- Metrics - Summary
- [Forward](https://docs.rs/struct.ForwardRequestMetrics.html)- Request - Metrics
- [Metrics](https://docs.rs/struct.MetricsDateFilter.html)- Date - Filter
- Date filter for metrics queries
- [Metrics](https://docs.rs/struct.MetricsSummary.html)- Summary
- Overall metrics summary
- [Model](https://docs.rs/struct.ModelMetrics.html)- Metrics
- Metrics aggregated by model
- [Round](https://docs.rs/struct.RoundMetrics.html)- Metrics
- Metrics for a single conversation round
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionDetail.html)- Detail
- Detailed session metrics with round information
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionMetrics.html)- Metrics
- Metrics for an entire session
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionMetricsFilter.html)- Metrics - Filter
- Filter for session metrics queries
- [Sqlite](https://docs.rs/struct.SqliteMetricsStorage.html)- Metrics - Storage
- SQLite-based implementation of the MetricsStorage trait.

# bamboo_infrastructure - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-infrastructure/2026.7.3/bamboo_infrastructure/

## Expand description

Bamboo infrastructure — process management, logging, and metrics.

This crate provides infrastructure-level utilities that are tightly coupled to the process environment (shell discovery, command building, window hiding).

Higher-level crates (LLM, config, storage, A2A) each have their own dedicated
crate (`bamboo-llm`, `bamboo-config`, `bamboo-storage`, `bamboo-a2a`) and should
be imported directly rather than through this crate.

# bamboo_compression - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-compression/2026.7.3/bamboo_compression/

## Expand description

Token budget management for LLM conversations.

This module provides token budget management to prevent context window overflow while maintaining conversation continuity. It implements a hybrid approach combining rolling summary with recent message windowing.

# ddd_cqrs_es - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ddd_cqrs_es/0.2.5/ddd_cqrs_es/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ddd_cqrs_es)ddd_cqrs_es

A lightweight framework for building Domain-Driven Design, CQRS, and Event Sourcing applications in Rust.

The crate provides explicit building blocks for aggregate command handling, optimistic concurrency, event replay, projections, process managers, snapshots, and pluggable persistence backends. The included in-memory store is intended for tests, examples, and local development.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ddd_cqrs_es::{Aggregate, DomainEvent, InMemoryEventStore, Metadata, Repository};
#[derive(Clone)]
enum CounterEvent {
    Created,
    Incremented(u64),
}
impl DomainEvent for CounterEvent {
    fn event_type(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            CounterEvent::Created => "counter_created",
            CounterEvent::Incremented(_) => "counter_incremented",
        }
    }
}
enum CounterCommand {
    Create,
    Increment(u64),
}
#[derive(Default)]
struct Counter {
    exists: bool,
    value: u64,
    revision: u64,
}
#[derive(Debug)]
enum CounterError {
    AlreadyCreated,
    NotCreated,
}
impl Aggregate for Counter {
    type Id = String;
    type Command = CounterCommand;
    type Event = CounterEvent;
    type Error = CounterError;
    fn aggregate_type() -> &'static str { "counter" }
    fn revision(&self) -> u64 { self.revision }
    fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }
    fn apply(&mut self, event: &Self::Event) {
        match event {
            CounterEvent::Created => self.exists = true,
            CounterEvent::Incremented(by) => self.value += by,
        }
        self.revision += 1;
    }
    fn handle(&self, command: Self::Command) -> Result<Vec<Self::Event>, Self::Error> {
        match command {
            CounterCommand::Create if self.exists => Err(CounterError::AlreadyCreated),
            CounterCommand::Create => Ok(vec![CounterEvent::Created]),
            CounterCommand::Increment(_) if !self.exists => Err(CounterError::NotCreated),
            CounterCommand::Increment(by) => Ok(vec![CounterEvent::Incremented(by)]),
        }
    }
}
let store = InMemoryEventStore::<Counter>::new();
let repo = Repository::new(store);
let counter_id = "counter-1".to_owned();
repo.execute(&counter_id, CounterCommand::Create, Metadata::default())?;
repo.execute(&counter_id, CounterCommand::Increment(5), Metadata::default())?;
let loaded = repo.load(&counter_id)?;
assert_eq!(loaded.state.value, 5);
```

# gpur 0.8.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gpur/0.8.1

# gpur

btop-style GPU monitor for the terminal. An `nvtop` replacement that runs
everywhere: NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple GPUs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

Mirrored braille waveforms, gradient meters, an nvtop-style process table with per-process GPU attribution, mouse support, foldable GPU cards, and theming via the hjkl stack.

Status: beta.The AMD Linux path is battle-tested on real hardware, and the macOS IOKit backend returns live data (validated against macOS CI runners' paravirt GPU — Apple Silicon numbers still welcome). Intel and Windows backends are implemented, CI-exercised, and awaiting real-GPU reports.

## Install

Debian/RPM packages, musl builds, and an Alpine `.apk` are attached to each
[GitHub release](https://github.com/kryptic-sh/gpur/releases).

## Run

## Keys & mouse

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| `q`/`Esc` | quit |
| `Space` | pause/resume polling |
| `0`-`9` | focus GPU list + select GPU N; same digit again folds it |
| `p` | focus process list |
| `j`/`k`, arrows | move within the focused pane |
| `J`/`K`, PgUp/PgDn | move the process cursor from anywhere |
| `s`/`r` | cycle process sort column / reverse it |
| `/` | filter processes (Enter applies, empty clears) |
| `x`/`X` | SIGTERM / SIGKILL the selected process (with confirm) |
| `+`/`=`/`-` | poll rate faster/slower |
| wheel / click | scroll + focus the pane under the cursor; click selects |

## Configuration

`gpur` reads `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gpur/config.toml` (falls back to
`~/.config/gpur/config.toml`). No file is written automatically; missing file
means built-in defaults.

```
 = 1000
 = 300
# graph glyphs: "braille" (default), "block", or "ascii" for fonts
# without braille coverage
 = "braille"
# hjkl-theme TOML; omit for the built-in theme
 = "/path/to/theme.toml"
```
Themes use the [hjkl-theme](https://crates.io/crates/hjkl-theme) schema:
`[palette]` of hex colors plus `[ui]` styles. Any hjkl theme file works — the
meters, waveform gradients, and highlights all derive from the palette.

## Backends

| Backend | Platform | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| nvml | Linux, Windows | NVML (dynamic load) | done |
| amdgpu | Linux | sysfs `/sys/class/drm`+ fdinfo | done |
| intel | Linux | i915/xe fdinfo + hwmon | done |
| pdh | Windows | GPU Engine/Adapter Memory + DXGI | done |
| ioaccel | macOS | IOAccelerator PerfStats (IOKit) | done |
| mock | all | deterministic waves ( `--mock`) | done |

Probe order: nvml → amdgpu → intel → ioaccel → pdh. Intel utilization is derived from per-client fdinfo engine counters (i915 busy-ns, xe cycles) the same way nvtop does it; power comes from the hwmon energy counter delta. PDH is the vendor-generic Windows fallback (Task Manager's counters) and reports utilization and memory only.

Backend poll failures degrade gracefully: the last snapshot stays on screen with a header warning until polling recovers — a driver reset won't kill the monitor.

Extras: each GPU card shows session peaks/averages (util, temp, power) when tall
enough, and the PCIe caption flags a link running below its maximum
(`PCIe 3.0@8x (max 4.0@16x)`) — a classic symptom of a bad riser or wrong slot.

Encoder/decoder activity shows in each card (split `enc`/`dec` on
NVIDIA/Windows, unified `video` on AMD/Intel), and a red throttle badge appears
when the GPU is thermal- or power-limited (real reasons on NVIDIA, at-limit
heuristic on AMD).

Planned depth: Apple temperature/power (SMC/IOReport), Windows AMD ADLX (temps/fans/clocks).

## Per-process GPU attribution

The process table (PID, user, device, type, GPU%, GPU memory, CPU%, host memory,
command) works on Linux (AMD + Intel via `/proc` fdinfo — same-user processes
unless run as root), NVIDIA everywhere (NVML), and Windows (PDH per-pid
counters). macOS has no public per-process GPU API. On Linux, containerized
processes get a CONTAINER column (docker/podman/k8s id from cgroups).

Recorded sessions replay: `gpur --log run.jsonl` while it happens, then
`gpur --replay run.jsonl` anywhere — including machines with no GPU — with the
recorded process attribution intact. Ideal for bug reports.

## License

MIT

# bamboo_broker - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-broker/2026.7.3/bamboo_broker/

## Expand description

`bamboo-broker` — a standalone network message broker for sub-agent
ask/reply (and future task/handoff) traffic.

The broker fronts durable per-session [ Mailbox](https://docs.rs/bamboo-subagent/2026.7.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bamboo_subagent/mailbox/struct.Mailbox.html)
queues with a WebSocket bus, so a central orchestrator and its workers —
local subprocesses, local Docker containers, or SSH/remote hosts — exchange
messages over the network with durability and at-least-once delivery, without
sharing a filesystem.

Topology: a single central broker (hub-and-spoke). It is a *pure message
bus* — it routes messages, it does not spawn actors or coordinate with other
brokers. Spawning the PUSH-side workers lives in [ deploy](https://docs.rs/deploy/index.html) (the

`Deployer`
family: local / docker / ssh / russh). (The `bamboo_subagent::WorkerLauncher`
trait that earlier docs referenced was never wired and has been removed; the
PULL-side actor runner dispatches placement inline.)Layers:

- `proto`
- `core`- `BrokerCore`
- the WebSocket server + auth + `bamboo broker serve`wiring layer on top (added next).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::ask::`- [ask_agent](https://docs.rs/ask/fn.ask_agent.html);
- `pub use crate::ask::`- [ask_over](https://docs.rs/ask/fn.ask_over.html);
- `pub use crate::ask::`- [request_over](https://docs.rs/ask/fn.request_over.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [ask](https://docs.rs/ask/index.html)
- Orchestrator-side ask: deliver an `Ask`to a target agent over the broker and await its correlated`Reply`. This is the primitive the`SubAgent`“ask” action (and tests) build on —`me`asks`target`a question and judges the answer, regardless of where`target`physically runs.
- [child_](https://docs.rs/child_link/index.html)- link
- `BrokerChildLink`— the parent side of running a child over the mailbox bus.
- [client](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)
- Broker client. Connects, does the `Hello`handshake, then runs a background reader that demuxes incoming frames into a`messages`stream and a`delivered`receipt stream — so one connection can both deliver and subscribe (the parent does both: deliver an Ask, subscribe for the Reply).
- [core](https://docs.rs/core/index.html)
- Broker routing core: per-session durable mailboxes + push subscriptions.
- [deploy](https://docs.rs/deploy/index.html)
- Deployers: bring up a `bamboo broker-agent serve`somewhere — as a local subprocess, in a Docker container, or on a remote host over SSH — pointed at a central broker. This is the orchestrator-side “push” model (the master deploys execution environments; workers dial home to the broker), as opposed to mutual discovery.
- [deploy_](https://docs.rs/deploy_russh/index.html)- russh
- `RusshDeployer`— deploy a- `broker-agent`worker over an in-process SSH connection (- `russh`- `ssh`cannot accept cleanly.
- [mcp](https://docs.rs/mcp/index.html)
- MCP-over-broker proxy (P2): a remote/deployed worker invokes host-bound MCP servers (e.g. nova — needs the screen/local creds) that physically run on the orchestrator, by forwarding the tool calls over the broker.
- [mux](https://docs.rs/mux/index.html)
- Request/reply MULTIPLEXER over a single broker connection.
- [proto](https://docs.rs/proto/index.html)
- Broker wire protocol: client ↔ broker frames, JSON over WebSocket text.
- [serve](https://docs.rs/serve/index.html)
- Mailbox serving loop: the worker side of the bus.
- [server](https://docs.rs/server/index.html)
- WebSocket server: a thin network shell over `BrokerCore`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Agent](https://docs.rs/struct.AgentRef.html)- Ref
- Sender identity attached to an inbox message.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Broker](https://docs.rs/enum.BrokerError.html)- Error
- Errors from broker operations.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [ORCHESTRATOR_](https://docs.rs/constant.ORCHESTRATOR_ID.html)- ID
- The orchestrator’s broker mailbox id — where workers send MCP proxy requests
and where `serve_mcp_proxy`listens. A fixed well-known id (single MCP host).

# ikigai_personal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ikigai-personal/0.3.1/ikigai_personal/

## Expand description

`ikigai-personal` — personal contexts for ikigai.

Late-bound, OS-backed resources under `urn:personal:*` — your contacts,
calendar, and free/busy availability — resolved through the local operating
system rather than a remote service, so the data never leaves the machine.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-support)Platform support

macOS is the first backend. **Windows and Linux are placeholders today**: the
crate *builds* on them, but the personal resources resolve to a clear
“not supported yet” error until their backends land (Windows: Microsoft Graph
/ Active Directory; Linux: LDAP / CalDAV / D-Bus). The macOS backend currently
returns clearly-labelled **sample data** pending the real Contacts/EventKit
integration.

[§](https://docs.rs#capability-scoping)Capability scoping

Access is gated by `urn:cap:` capability scopes (see `ikigai-core`’s
`Capability`). `urn:personal:calendar` projects on the capability: a holder of
`urn:cap:personal:calendar:read:detail` sees full detail; one with only
`…:read:freebusy` sees busy blocks (no titles or attendees); one with neither
is denied. That’s the data-minimization story — *“an agent books around my
week without ever learning what I’m doing”* — and it’s why detail and free/busy
are one resource with two capability-scoped views rather than two resources.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Calendar](https://docs.rs/struct.CalendarConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for the consolidated-view calendar machinery — the
hand-editable file a host loads (conventionally
`~/.config/ikigai/calendar.json`).
- [Calendar](https://docs.rs/struct.CalendarInfo.html)- Info
- One native calendar, as the OS reports it.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventInfo.html)- Info
- One calendar event, normalized from the OS store.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [availability](https://docs.rs/fn.availability.html)
- `availability`: the free/busy projection for a period — busy blocks only, gated on- `urn:cap:personal:calendar:read:freebusy`.
- [calendar](https://docs.rs/fn.calendar.html)
- `calendar`: real events for a period, projected on the capability — full detail with- `…:read:detail`(and a Turtle face via- `as=text/turtle`), free/busy with- `…:read:freebusy`, denied with neither.
- [calendar_](https://docs.rs/fn.calendar_config.html)- config
- `calendar:config`: the effective consolidated-view configuration the host loaded (view name, source allowlist, inbox, account) — or a pointer to create the file if none was found.
- [calendars](https://docs.rs/fn.calendars.html)
- `calendars`: the native calendar collection.- `Source`lists every calendar with its account;- `Sink`creates one —- `name=`(default: the configured view) on- `account=`(default: configured account, else iCloud, else the system default). Real EventKit; the first use may raise the macOS calendar-access prompt.
- [contacts](https://docs.rs/fn.contacts.html)
- `contacts`: the local address book, gated on- `urn:cap:personal:contacts:read`.
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_supported.html)- supported
- Whether a personal backend is implemented for the platform this was built for.
- [platform_](https://docs.rs/fn.platform_name.html)- name
- The human-readable name of the platform this was built for.
- [space](https://docs.rs/fn.space.html)
- The personal-contexts space: binds the resources at `urn:personal:*`. The optional`CalendarConfig``~/.config/ikigai/calendar.json`) parameterizes the consolidated-view machinery;`None`leaves the read resources fully functional.

# bamboo_subagent - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bamboo-subagent/2026.7.3/bamboo_subagent/

## Expand description

`bamboo-subagent` — sub-agent fleet runtime.

Slice 1 (this build): pure filesystem logic, no runtime dependency.

- `store`
- `mailbox`

See `docs/subagent-actor-runtime-design.md` (§3.4, §5) and
`docs/subagent-store-mailbox-interface.md` for the design these implement.

The session payload is kept opaque (generic `T: Serialize`/`DeserializeOwned`) so this
crate stays a leaf and is fully unit-testable with a tempdir; higher layers pass the
domain `Session`. Index rebuild is decoupled via the [ store::MetaExtractor](https://docs.rs/store/trait.MetaExtractor.html) seam.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [discovery](https://docs.rs/discovery/index.html)
- Tier-1 discovery: a process-independent, file-based fabric (design §4).
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error model + atomic write helper shared by `store`and`mailbox`.
- [executor](https://docs.rs/executor/index.html)
- The `ChildExecutor`seam: how an actor actually runs a task.
- [fleet](https://docs.rs/fleet/index.html)
- Parent-side fleet helpers: spawn an actor subprocess, provision it over stdin, discover it.
- [mailbox](https://docs.rs/mailbox/index.html)
- Maildir-style persistent mailbox (design §3.4).
- [proto](https://docs.rs/proto/index.html)
- Wire protocol: discovery record + parent/child WebSocket frames.
- [provision](https://docs.rs/provision/index.html)
- ProvisionSpec — the one-shot bootstrap contract between parent and worker.
- [store](https://docs.rs/store/index.html)
- Project-keyed session store + denormalized indices.
- [transport](https://docs.rs/transport/index.html)
- WebSocket transport (design §6): full-duplex parent↔child link.

# Heap in linked_list_allocator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/linked_list_allocator/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/linked_list_allocator/struct.Heap.html

`pub struct Heap { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A fixed size heap backed by a linked list of free memory blocks.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Initializes an empty heap

The `heap_bottom` pointer is automatically aligned, so the [ bottom()](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.bottom)
method might return a pointer that is larger than

`heap_bottom` after construction.The given `heap_size` must be large enough to store the required
metadata, otherwise this function will panic. Depending on the
alignment of the `hole_addr` pointer, the minimum size is between
`2 * size_of::<usize>` and `3 * size_of::<usize>`.

The usable size for allocations will be truncated to the nearest
alignment of `align_of::<usize>`. Any extra bytes left at the end
will be reclaimed once sufficient additional space is given to
[ extend](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.extend).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This function must be called at most once and must only be used on an empty heap.

The bottom address must be valid and the memory in the
`[heap_bottom, heap_bottom + heap_size)` range must not be used for anything else.
This function is unsafe because it can cause undefined behavior if the given address
is invalid.

The provided memory range must be valid for the `'static` lifetime.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#115-128)#### pub fn [init_from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.init_from_slice)(&mut self, mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>])

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#115-128)

#### pub fn [init_from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.init_from_slice)(&mut self, mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>])

Initialize an empty heap with provided memory.

The caller is responsible for procuring a region of raw memory that may be utilized by the allocator. This might be done via any method such as (unsafely) taking a region from the program’s memory, from a mutable static, or by allocating and leaking such memory from another allocator.

The latter approach may be especially useful if the underlying allocator does not perform deallocation (e.g. a simple bump allocator). Then the overlaid linked-list-allocator can provide memory reclamation.

The usable size for allocations will be truncated to the nearest
alignment of `align_of::<usize>`. Any extra bytes left at the end
will be reclaimed once sufficient additional space is given to
[ extend](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.extend).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This method panics if the heap is already initialized.

It also panics when the length of the given `mem` slice is not large enough to
store the required metadata. Depending on the alignment of the slice, the minimum
size is between `2 * size_of::<usize>` and `3 * size_of::<usize>`.

Creates a new heap with the given `bottom` and `size`.

The `heap_bottom` pointer is automatically aligned, so the [ bottom()](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.bottom)
method might return a pointer that is larger than

`heap_bottom` after construction.The given `heap_size` must be large enough to store the required
metadata, otherwise this function will panic. Depending on the
alignment of the `hole_addr` pointer, the minimum size is between
`2 * size_of::<usize>` and `3 * size_of::<usize>`.

The usable size for allocations will be truncated to the nearest
alignment of `align_of::<usize>`. Any extra bytes left at the end
will be reclaimed once sufficient additional space is given to
[ extend](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.extend).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-1)Safety

The bottom address must be valid and the memory in the
`[heap_bottom, heap_bottom + heap_size)` range must not be used for anything else.
This function is unsafe because it can cause undefined behavior if the given address
is invalid.

The provided memory range must be valid for the `'static` lifetime.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#165-171)#### pub fn [from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.from_slice)(mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>]) -> [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#165-171)

#### pub fn [from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.from_slice)(mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>]) -> [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html)

Creates a new heap from a slice of raw memory.

This is a convenience function that has the same effect as calling
[`init_from_slice`] on an empty heap. All the requirements of `init_from_slice`
apply to this function as well.

Allocates a chunk of the given size with the given alignment. Returns a pointer to the
beginning of that chunk if it was successful. Else it returns `None`.
This function scans the list of free memory blocks and uses the first block that is big
enough. The runtime is in O(n) where n is the number of free blocks, but it should be
reasonably fast for small allocations.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#203-205)#### pub unsafe fn [deallocate](https://docs.rs#method.deallocate)(&mut self, ptr: [NonNull](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/non_null/struct.NonNull.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>, layout: [Layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/alloc/layout/struct.Layout.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#203-205)

#### pub unsafe fn [deallocate](https://docs.rs#method.deallocate)(&mut self, ptr: [NonNull](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/non_null/struct.NonNull.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>, layout: [Layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/alloc/layout/struct.Layout.html))

Frees the given allocation. `ptr` must be a pointer returned
by a call to the `allocate_first_fit` function with identical size and alignment.

This function walks the list of free memory blocks and inserts the freed block at the
correct place. If the freed block is adjacent to another free block, the blocks are merged
again. This operation is in `O(n)` since the list needs to be sorted by address.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-2)Safety

`ptr` must be a pointer returned by a call to the [`allocate_first_fit`] function with
identical layout. Undefined behavior may occur for invalid arguments.

Returns the bottom address of the heap.

The bottom pointer is automatically aligned, so the returned pointer might be larger than the bottom pointer used for initialization.

Return the top address of the heap.

Note: The heap may choose to not use bytes at the end for allocations
until there is enough room for metadata, but it still retains ownership
over memory from [ bottom](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.bottom) to the address returned.

Extends the size of the heap by creating a new hole at the end.

Small extensions are not guaranteed to grow the usable size of
the heap. In order to grow the Heap most effectively, extend by
at least `2 * size_of::<usize>`, keeping the amount a multiple of
`size_of::<usize>`.

Calling this method on an uninitialized Heap will panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-3)Safety

The amount of data given in `by` MUST exist directly after the original
range of data provided when constructing the [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html). The additional data
must have the same lifetime of the original range of data.

Even if this operation doesn’t increase the [usable size](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.size)
by exactly `by` bytes, those bytes are still owned by the Heap for
later use.

alignment of the `hole_addr` pointer, the minimum size is between
`2 * size_of::<usize>` and `3 * size_of::<usize>`.

The usable size for allocations will be truncated to the nearest
alignment of `align_of::<usize>`. Any extra bytes left at the end
will be reclaimed once sufficient additional space is given to
[ extend](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.extend).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-1)Safety

The bottom address must be valid and the memory in the
`[heap_bottom, heap_bottom + heap_size)` range must not be used for anything else.
This function is unsafe because it can cause undefined behavior if the given address
is invalid.

The provided memory range must be valid for the `'static` lifetime.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#165-171)#### pub fn [from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.from_slice)(mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>]) -> [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#165-171)

#### pub fn [from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.from_slice)(mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>]) -> [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html)

Creates a new heap from a slice of raw memory.

This is a convenience function that has the same effect as calling
[`init_from_slice`] on an empty heap. All the requirements of `init_from_slice`
apply to this function as well.

Allocates a chunk of the given size with the given alignment. Returns a pointer to the
beginning of that chunk if it was successful. Else it returns `None`.
This function scans the list of free memory blocks and uses the first block that is big
enough. The runtime is in O(n) where n is the number of free blocks, but it should be
reasonably fast for small allocations.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#203-205)#### pub unsafe fn [deallocate](https://docs.rs#method.deallocate)(&mut self, ptr: [NonNull](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/non_null/struct.NonNull.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>, layout: [Layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/alloc/layout/struct.Layout.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#203-205)

#### pub unsafe fn [deallocate](https://docs.rs#method.deallocate)(&mut self, ptr: [NonNull](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ptr/non_null/struct.NonNull.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>, layout: [Layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/alloc/layout/struct.Layout.html))

Frees the given allocation. `ptr` must be a pointer returned
by a call to the `allocate_first_fit` function with identical size and alignment.

This function walks the list of free memory blocks and inserts the freed block at the
correct place. If the freed block is adjacent to another free block, the blocks are merged
again. This operation is in `O(n)` since the list needs to be sorted by address.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-2)Safety

`ptr` must be a pointer returned by a call to the [`allocate_first_fit`] function with
identical layout. Undefined behavior may occur for invalid arguments.

Returns the bottom address of the heap.

The bottom pointer is automatically aligned, so the returned pointer might be larger than the bottom pointer used for initialization.

Return the top address of the heap.

Note: The heap may choose to not use bytes at the end for allocations
until there is enough room for metadata, but it still retains ownership
over memory from [ bottom](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.bottom) to the address returned.

Extends the size of the heap by creating a new hole at the end.

Small extensions are not guaranteed to grow the usable size of
the heap. In order to grow the Heap most effectively, extend by
at least `2 * size_of::<usize>`, keeping the amount a multiple of
`size_of::<usize>`.

Calling this method on an uninitialized Heap will panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-3)Safety

The amount of data given in `by` MUST exist directly after the original
range of data provided when constructing the [Heap](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html). The additional data
must have the same lifetime of the original range of data.

Even if this operation doesn’t increase the [usable size](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.size)
by exactly `by` bytes, those bytes are still owned by the Heap for
later use.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/linked_list_allocator/lib.rs.html#115-128)#### pub fn [init_from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.init_from_slice)(&mut self, mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>])

#### pub fn [init_from_slice](https://docs.rs#method.init_from_slice)(&mut self, mem: &'static mut [[MaybeUninit](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/maybe_uninit/union.MaybeUninit.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.u8.html)>])

Initialize an empty heap with provided memory.

The caller is responsible for procuring a region of raw memory that may be utilized by the allocator. This might be done via any method such as (unsafely) taking a region from the program’s memory, from a mutable static, or by allocating and leaking such memory from another allocator.

The latter approach may be especially useful if the underlying allocator does not perform deallocation (e.g. a simple bump allocator). Then the overlaid linked-list-allocator can provide memory reclamation.

The usable size for allocations will be truncated to the nearest
alignment of `align_of::<usize>`. Any extra bytes left at the end
will be reclaimed once sufficient additional space is given to
[ extend](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.extend).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This method panics if the heap is already initialized.

It also panics when the length of the given `mem` slice is not large enough to
store the required metadata. Depending on the alignment of the slice, the minimum
size is between `2 * size_of::<usize>` and `3 * size_of::<usize>`.

Creates a new heap with the given `bottom` and `size`.

The `heap_bottom` pointer is automatically aligned, so the [ bottom()](https://docs.rs/struct.Heap.html#method.bottom)
method might return a pointer that is larger than

`heap_bottom` after construction.The given `heap_size` must be large enough to store the required
metadata, otherwise this function will panic. Depending on the
alignment of the `hole_addr` pointer, the minimum size is between

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
